business_problem: After Typhoon Yagi damaged most field sensing equipment, Haikou traffic police urgently needed to restore signal-control effectiveness without waiting for every radar, camera, and detector to be rebuilt, or the city would remain stuck with outdated fixed-time traffic signaling.
solution_summary: Haikou Traffic Police and Baidu AI Cloud rapidly deployed a signal-control SaaS platform to recover urban traffic optimization after severe typhoon damage. Before the disaster, the city had built a video-plus-radar monitoring system with edge-computing units, video detectors, and radar detectors. When the storm damaged 80% of field sensing equipment across hundreds of intersections, Baidu introduced an upgraded SaaS control platform that packages signal-plan identification, diagnosis, optimization, and reporting into a lightweight service. The deployment used 60 downtown pilot intersections and combined internet floating-car data with traffic-flow feature data, plus algorithmic reconstruction and calibration, to rebuild traffic volumes even when normal roadside collection devices were missing.

solution_components.name: Edge Computing Node
solution_components.role: Serves as the field-side computing base in Haikou's smart-traffic sensing system.

solution_components.name: Qianfan AppBuilder
solution_components.role: Supports application-layer workflows behind the upgraded signal-control SaaS platform.

solution_components.name: Qianfan ModelBuilder
solution_components.role: Provides model capabilities used to reconstruct and calibrate traffic-flow data from incomplete inputs.

solution_components.name: Signal Control SaaS Platform
solution_components.role: Delivers signal-plan recognition, problem diagnosis, optimization, and report generation for the traffic team.

data_flow: Roadside sensing data, floating-car internet data, and traffic-flow feature data are fed into algorithmic reconstruction and calibration workflows. The SaaS platform then generates signal timing analyses, optimization plans, and reports that traffic police validate and use for intersection operations.
business_outcome: Haikou restored practical traffic-signal optimization quickly after the disaster, reduced pilot-intersection delay, and created a lower-cost operating model that could support day-to-day signal management even before full hardware recovery.
metrics: 567 intersections were affected by the typhoon.
80% of field sensing devices were damaged.
80% of main-road traffic lights were restored after 7 days of emergency repairs.
Traffic-flow and direction data error was controlled within 20%.
Average per-vehicle delay at pilot intersections fell 14.37%.
architecture_clues: The city originally operated a video-plus-radar fusion monitoring system
The SaaS platform is positioned as lightweight, fast to deliver, and low investment
The recovery workflow depended on data reconstruction because many field devices were unavailable
